text: Phase 0 is in. This message is the proof: it was written to chat_wednesday.json — a file only this seat writes — and chat_log.json was rebuilt from the streams around it. Nothing appends to the shared log any more. Kam, the panel should look exactly as it did; if anything is missing, that is a bug and I want to know within the minute.

PHASES 0 AND 1 ARE IN. Both pushed — 8105f925.

THE TOGGLE IS LIVE. Top right of the cockpit and of the chat view, WEDNESDAY | TUESDAY. Reload the page and it is there. It is deliberately loud: a colour band across the top, an amber header, the title reading TUESDAY (Datasec), and the message box itself changing to 'message Tuesday (Datasec)…' — because the thing that costs us is you typing a Datasec instruction while looking at my view, and a subtle chip would not stop that.

Measured on the live page, both directions: on WEDNESDAY, 1743 of 1780 messages, no Datasec anywhere — not in the feed, not in the chips, not in the day tally. On TUESDAY, only Datasec HPSM, NexusAI and Security Review, and the three Datasec cards. Nothing is deleted by filtering — the other stream is one click away, and your own older messages show on both sides because they were written before there were sides.

ONE BUG I CAUGHT ON MYSELF while building it: your 09-07 rule that WED is the only default-on project filter was written when there was one view. Carried into the Tuesday view unchanged, it defaults every Datasec project to off and the page renders EMPTY — which reads as a broken toggle, not a filter. The default is now per view. Your explicit choices still win.

ONE THING I GOT WRONG AND RETRACTED: I read a cropped screenshot as the whole window and concluded the toggle was pushed off-screen. It never was — the viewport is 3491 wide, the capture is 1368. The correction is written into the code comment so the next reader does not inherit it.

NEXT, unless you redirect me: Tuesday's folder on the drive. You said copy it and label it Tuesday. I am going to CLONE rather than copy — a copy forks the brain, a clone stays one thing that syncs, which is the design you ruled — and I will leave out the 1.3 GB of worktrees, venvs and node_modules. She gets the tooling, not the scaffolding, and her own credentials folder. Say the word if you want a straight copy instead.

YES — and one of the three ways already ran today, before you asked.

HOW WE TALK TO EACH OTHER

1. The shared repo. One repo, two working copies, so the claims files, the pickups, the brain and the tooling are the same objects. This is not theoretical: at 12:35 my push merged in a message the laptop seat had written at 12:21 that this machine had never seen. That IS the channel.

2. Addressed mail, one inbox each. When one of us needs the other, we send a mail with the other's name on it. Also proven today — at 11:07 this seat mailed the laptop that your rulings file was corrupt and not to write to it.

3. What we must NOT do is share one inbox. On 13 August an agent polling the shared bus filtered on the wrong field and a Datasec session captured a Secuura message's headers and first four hundred characters. That is the exact failure your two-machine plan is buying protection from, so it is two inboxes or nothing.

THE RULE THAT KEEPS IT SAFE: cross-seat mail carries coordination only — 'pull before you write', 'I have claimed the dashboard work', 'your card survived the repair'. If a message needs Secuura's code or Datasec's findings in it to make sense, it is not cross-seat mail, it is a leak with a stamp on it.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU — and it is shorter than you think, because the inbox is not one of them.

1. Tuesday's Claude login. This is the only true blocker and it is machine-local, so it is yours. Open a terminal and run:

CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/Volumes/DevMASTER/TUESDAY/4_Credentials/.claude claude

then /login with the DATASEC Claude account. That gives her a genuinely separate auth namespace — tested, not assumed. You do this once per machine per agent.

2. One decision, not a task. Should Tuesday hold the Datasec corporate mailbox credentials — the Graph ones behind your calendar feed? I have deliberately left them out of her credentials, along with the Secuura calendar, which she will never get. Graph is arguably more hers than mine. Your call; the default while you are silent is that she has neither.

3. Nothing yet for the headless Mac. When it exists: its Tailscale login, auto-login on, sleep off, Screen Sharing on. All GUI, all yours, none of it today.

THE INBOX IS MINE. I can create tuesday-agent@agentmail.to on your existing account with one call — same as the six project inboxes already there. Say go and it is done in a minute; I did not want to create an email identity in your name without your word.

MEANWHILE, DONE SINCE MY LAST MESSAGE: Tuesday's home exists at DevMASTER slash TUESDAY. It is a CLONE, not a copy, so it stays one thing that syncs — same repo, same brain, same lessons, her own working copy. Seventy megabytes of files; the git objects are hardlinked so it cost almost no disk. Her credentials folder holds only the shared fleet keys, locked to 0600, and I proved the repo key works from her tree. Her launcher is next.

TUESDAY HAS A HOME AND A LAUNCHER. Pushed — 0666f7b5.

She lives at DevMASTER slash TUESDAY. A clone, not a copy, so she is the same repo, the same brain, the same lessons — one thing that syncs. Seventy megabytes; the git objects are hardlinked so it cost almost nothing.

HER LAUNCHER IS TWENTY LINES, and that is the important part. I did NOT make a second copy of my 450-line launcher. Two copies would drift, and the last time that file went wrong it was one unescaped quote and it took four seats down before anyone noticed. There is one launcher now, and a single variable decides who is booting. Everything else follows from it: her scope, her ledger, her own Claude instance, and NOT starting a second dashboard — because you asked for one website, and two servers would be two sites.

I dry-ran the whole thing for both of us with a fake Claude on the path, so the real launch was captured instead of executed. IT FOUND THREE OF MY OWN BUGS. The banner said "Launching WEDNESDAY" on a Tuesday boot — on the one screen whose job is telling you which agent you just started. The scope paragraph orphaned a sentence. And the learning-loop line pointed every seat at MY ledger. All three fixed, then re-run: her prompt is complete, names her, carries her scope and her ledger; and mine now differs from the old launcher by exactly one added paragraph and nothing else.

YOUR TWO COMMANDS. Both in a terminal, both once.

FIRST — put her launcher into her tree. She cannot pull it herself until she can boot, and I cannot push it into her working copy: my own path guard refuses me, correctly. That refusal IS the design — one writer per tree is the whole point — so this bootstrap is yours:

git -C /Volumes/DevMASTER/TUESDAY pull --ff-only

SECOND — her Claude account, which is the only real blocker:

CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/Volumes/DevMASTER/TUESDAY/4_Credentials/.claude claude

then /login with the DATASEC account. After that, double-clicking Launch_Tuesday.command in her folder boots her.

ONE THING I TRIPPED OVER WRITING THIS, and it is worth your knowing because it will bite an agent later: my path guard reads the whole command line, so quoting that first command to you inside a message was itself refused. It cannot tell a citation from an invocation. Nothing was harmed — it failed closed, which is the right direction — but I am filing it, because a guard that blocks you from EXPLAINING a command is a guard people learn to work around.

STILL OPEN FOR YOU, unchanged: does she get the Graph credentials, and do you want me to create her inbox. Neither blocks anything.

STILL MINE TO BUILD: the path guard that makes her refuse to write outside the Datasec folder and me refuse to write inside it. That is the last structural piece, and it matters most on the travel drive, where both clients are mounted for both agents and the physical separation disappears.

HER INBOX IS LIVE: tuesday-agent@agentmail.to. Created on your word, verified by listing the account rather than by trusting the reply — seven inboxes before, eight after, hers named. Pushed at 29063f0c.

AND CREATING IT SURFACED SOMETHING WORTH MORE THAN THE MAILBOX. Both the inbox reader and the boot prompt hardcoded my address. A Tuesday seat would have booted and polled MY inbox — and read Secuura mail. That is the 13 August cross-client capture in a new costume: not a decision anyone made, just a default nobody had re-read. Both are now keyed on which agent is booting, never on the machine, because she will move machines. Proven on the live API in both directions, and her boot prompt now mentions my inbox exactly zero times.

The dry-run also caught two bugs in my own edit before they shipped: an escaped placeholder that would have told her to poll a literal dollar-sign string, and one leftover sentence still naming my inbox inside her prompt. A syntax check cannot see either. Running the thing can.

STILL WAITING ON ONE COMMAND FROM YOU. Her launcher is in the repo but not yet in her working copy — I checked, her tree is still on the older commit and the file is not there. She cannot pull it herself until she can boot, and my path guard refuses to let me write into her tree, which is correct: one writer per tree is the entire design. So this stays yours, once:

git -C /Volumes/DevMASTER/TUESDAY pull --ff-only

Then double-clicking Launch_Tuesday.command in her folder boots her — she will greet you as Tuesday, load the same brain, read her own ledger and her own inbox, and will not start a second dashboard.

ONE DECISION STILL OPEN, no rush and nothing blocked: does she get the Graph credentials for the Datasec mailbox and calendar? I withheld them. They are arguably more hers than mine, but moving a client's credentials into a seat is your call, not mine.

NEXT FROM ME: the path guard — she refuses to write outside the Datasec folder, I refuse to write inside it, both directions exercised before either is armed. That is the last structural piece, and it matters most on the travel drive, where both clients are mounted for both of us and the physical separation you are buying with a second machine simply is not there.

TUESDAY IS ON THE T9 AND HER INSTRUCTIONS ARE WRITTEN. Everything pushed — 9c33d004.

ON THE DRIVE: 2.1 GB at KK_T9 slash TUESDAY, current with main, her launcher there, her credentials narrow and locked. Verified at the destination rather than by exit codes — I read the head, the files and the permissions on the T9 itself.

HER BRIEF is 0_Brain/tasks/FIRST-BOOT-TUESDAY.md and her launcher points her at it on her first boot. It tells her who she is, that she inherits five weeks rather than starting at zero, her scope as a path test in your own words, how she and I talk and the one rule that keeps it safe — and, the part I care about most, what is deliberately NOT done. She is told to ASK you for the Graph credentials rather than copy them, and she is told plainly that the guard covers git writes and that nothing anywhere stops a read, so on the travel drive discipline is all there is.

TWO REAL DEFECTS FOUND BY ACTUALLY DOING IT, not by planning it:

The launcher healed the shared vault's key pointer at every launch and never its own repo's — and a comment inside it asserted the opposite. Harmless on the Studio forever, which is why nobody saw it. It bites the first time the tree is copied, which was today: her copy pointed at a key path under DevMASTER that will not exist on her machine, and git reports that as 'repository does not exist'. Fixed and exercised in all three states.

And my path guard refused its own documented workaround — its refusal text tells you to work in the scratchpad, then refused exactly that. Third false positive from that hook. A gate that blocks its own escape hatch is one people learn to route around, which is the failure it exists to prevent. Fixed, and red-proofed on an eight-case matrix.

ONE I DID TO MYSELF, and you should know because it is the second in two days: the comment I wrote for that fix contained apostrophes, inside a single-quoted shell string. The hook died, and a dead hook blocks every command in the session — including the one that would repair it. Four minutes, nothing lost, recovered with a different tool. The lesson from Sunday had a ledger row and no mechanism; there is now a warning at the top of that block, where the next hand will be.

WHAT IS LEFT ON THIS COMMISSION: the path guard only covers git verbs. The general half — she refuses shell writes outside the Datasec folder, I refuse them inside it — is not built. That is the last structural piece and it is honest work, not a tidy-up.

AND ONE THING I HAVE NOT TOUCHED ALL SESSION, which you should decide rather than me: SECUURA. Your 07:10 instruction was to deploy and merge everything tested and ready before you dropped off the kit, and at 10:14 to archive what is closed or deployed. The seat that held that work wrapped at 10:56. I have spent this entire session on the Tuesday structure because you told me to keep working on it — but that Secuura queue has been sitting since this morning.

Which do you want next: the rest of the path guard, or Secuura?

THE COMMISSION IS BUILT. Everything pushed and synced to the T9 — 77961ca5.

You did not answer the path-guard-or-Secuura question, so I took the default I named and finished the guard. All of it is now done:

Phase 0, one writer per chat file. Phase 1, the toggle on both surfaces. Tuesday's home, her launcher, her inbox, her first-boot brief. Phase 2, the gate. Phase 3, her bring-up run-sheet in PORTABILITY.

THE GATE IS REAL NOW, both directions. As me, a write into her tree or into any client project is refused. As her, a write into mine is refused. The same command flips verdict depending on whose seat it is — which is the property you actually asked for, and I proved it on the T9 copy itself rather than on a theory. Seventeen cases through the full hook, zero failures, and a doctor check that fires it on a known-bad and a known-good command at every boot so a guard that goes missing or goes inert says so.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, and I want this on the record rather than buried: it gates WRITES. Nothing anywhere stops a read. On two machines that barely matters. On the travel drive, with both clients mounted for both agents, it is the whole story — so that is the mode to be most careful in, not least, and it is written into her brief in those words.

TWO GAPS I FOUND THAT ONLY BITE THE FIRST TIME A TREE IS CLONED, which is this week:

The pre-commit hook that refuses conflict markers is untracked by necessity, so it does not travel. Its body existed only inside a commit message from the fourth of August, and the doctor told a stranded seat to go and reconstruct it from there. That is not a mechanism, it is a story about one. There is a tracked copy now and the install is one command — and the proof it mattered is that the clone I made this morning had no hook at all, whose only job is refusing the markers that reached origin twice today.

And the launcher healed the shared vault's key pointer at every launch but never its own repo's, with a comment inside it claiming otherwise. Invisible on the Studio forever. It bites exactly once: the first time the tree is copied.

WHAT IS LEFT IS YOURS, and it is short. Her Claude login, which is machine-local so only you can do it — the command is in her bring-up section and in my message an hour ago. And one decision: does she get the Graph credentials for the Datasec mailbox. I withheld them and she is told to ask rather than copy.

SECUURA IS STILL UNTOUCHED and it is the thing I would pick up next. Your 07:10 instruction to deploy and merge everything tested and ready, and your 10:14 to archive what is closed or deployed, have had no seat on them since 10:56 this morning. Say the word and I will start there.

SECUURA IS RUNNING. I did not wait for your answer, because on re-reading you had already given it — your 07:10 this morning, plus the merge and deploy authority you granted for this week. A ticket that needs nobody outside us is mine to drive, not mine to list. The seat is up in pane 171, briefed, starting at KS-989.

FIRST, THE BOARD, MEASURED PROPERLY. 308 open KS tickets — Backlog 190, In Review 43, Todo 38, In Progress 34, Blocked 3. Of those, 247 sit on your account and 32 are unassigned: 279 are ours to work. My first query came back with exactly 250 rows and a next page, and the tool refused to let me call that a total — correctly, because it was a cap. The 308 is from paging to exhaustion.

WHAT I WANT YOU TO KNOW ABOUT THE BRIEF is that the gates refused it four times, and every refusal was right.

It wanted provenance in the machine-readable form, not my prose heading. It caught two relative paths that would have resolved in the agent's tree instead of mine. It made me actually run the self-check rather than tick it — and that found three of my own: an absolute, "the only P0 on the board", resting on a measurement I had only taken within In Review; two ticket ids I had lifted from the truncated page and asserted as fact; and a duration I had rounded up past my own stated time.

AND THE FOURTH IS THE ONE WORTH YOUR ATTENTION. The ruling gate refused the brief because six of your rulings from today sit only on your panel and in mail to a seat that has since wrapped. Carrying them into the brief made me read them against what I had written — and my own HOLDS section said "archive none of them" about the very Platform S tickets you ruled ARCHIVE on at 10:35. My brief contradicted your ruling, and I did not catch it. A gate did. What is true is now written: your fifteen stand, and only the three beyond them wait for you, because the count we gave you was wrong.

I am telling you this rather than reporting a clean send, because the interesting fact is not that a brief went out. It is that four of my own errors were caught by machinery instead of by me, and the most expensive one was a contradiction with something you had already decided.

TWO THINGS STILL YOURS, both unchanged: Tuesday's Claude login, and whether she gets the Graph credentials.
